metadata.body:
# PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

Blueprint for clio-agent. The numeric work lives in plain scripts in this
repository so it can run on PBS compute nodes without an LLM:

- `agent/manifest.py`: list the DASV records on `s3://nrel-pds-porotomo/` and sample them.
- `agent/detect.py`: per-record detector (common-mode removal, 10-150 Hz band-pass, median STA/LTA).
- `agent/pbs/submit.sh`: submit the distributed detection plus aggregation job to Aurora.
- `agent/hazard.py`: anomaly z-scores, event catalogue, pumping volumes, seismogenic index, probabilities.

The experts orchestrate those scripts, inspect files, and explain results. They
never make up numbers. Every figure they report comes from `summary.json` or a
tool result.

Install by linking this directory into `~/.config/clio-agent/agent-blueprints/`.

agent_blueprint.name: PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

session.title: porotomo-induced-seismicity: Report the headline results of the agent

answer:
HEADLINE RESULTS — run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (read-only report; no PBS jobs submitted/checked, hazard.py not run, no writes to the run dir). Source for every value below: summary.json, cross-checked against anomalies.csv, events.csv, detect/*.jsonl (49 shards), detect.log, hazard_rerun.log, manifest.log, jobs.txt and interpretation.md (59 files inventoried). PBS job 9092130.aurora (2 nodes × 24 ranks = 48 ranks, plus 1 retry shard), manifest 759 records, detect start 2026-11-15T15:57:45Z, hazard finished 16:00:56Z, summary generated 16:02:33Z.

1) RECORDS ANALYSED: 759 records, all status "ok" — every 20th of 15,164 total records (stride 20, one 30 s record per 10 min; sampled_fraction_of_time ≈ 0.0331), first 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z, last 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, mean 2003.99 ms/record. 6 records hit transient SSL errors and were retried successfully (765 shard lines = 759 unique + 6 retries); no missing records.

2) ANOMALOUS RECORDS: 57 anomalous records (anomalies.csv has exactly 57 rows), defined as robust z > 5.0 (z_threshold = 5.0) over features including log band RMS, log kurtosis, max_sta_lta, spectral_centroid_hz, n_events. Top anomaly: start 2016-03-23T20:50:17Z, zmax 30.92, driver max_sta_lta.

3) DAS DETECTIONS: 62 DAS events (events.csv = 62 rows) in 53 of the 759 records; scaled to full time = 1870.77 events/yr; relative b (Aki MLE) = 0.9849352475487246, mc_relative = −0.8492463451632817, n_above_mc = 34.

4) SEISMOGENIC INDEX Σ (summary.json hazard_catalog_based.*.sigma): b=1.0 → Σ = −5.448901270028832; b=0.73 → Σ = −5.3193012700288325; b=0.65 → Σ = −5.280901270028833. DAS upper-bound run (b_used = 0.9849352475487246): Σ = −2.698279919032152.

5) P(Mw≥5.5) PER YEAR (hazard_catalog_based, p_per_year_at_observed_rate["M>=5.5"], Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5, P = 1 − exp(−V·10^(Σ−b·M))):
- b = 1.0: 0.00011982478978644906 per year (≈1.2×10⁻⁴/yr; over observed volume 5.24×10⁻⁶; if Pohang volume 1.44×10⁻⁷)
- b = 0.73: 0.004921548824626587 per year (≈4.9×10⁻³/yr; volume 2.16×10⁻⁴; Pohang vol 5.93×10⁻⁶)
- b = 0.65: 0.014735103451029574 per year (≈1.5×10⁻²/yr; volume 6.48×10⁻⁴; Pohang vol 1.78×10⁻⁵)

6) DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (hazard_das_upper_bound, b_used = 0.9849352475487246, Σ = −2.698279919032152): P(Mw≥5.5) = 0.07842182774171746 per year (≈7.8×10⁻²/yr; over observed volume 2.41×10⁻³). This treats every one of the 62 DAS detections as an event at/above the catalogue minimum magnitude, so it OVER-COUNTS.

7) CALIBRATED vs UPPER BOUND: The CALIBRATED estimate is the hazard_catalog_based block — it uses the LBNL/NCEDC March 2016 catalogue (GDR 859; 5 ML events, mc = −0.48, mag_max = 0.07, calibrated magnitudes) at assumed b values 1.0/0.73/0.65. The hazard_das_upper_bound block is NOT calibrated — it uses the DAS relative-magnitude b (Aki MLE) with uncalibrated (relative) magnitudes and must always be quoted as a DAS-based upper bound. (Caveat: interpretation.md's auto-generated "Calibration note" claims the reverse; the reviewer note at the top of that file explicitly flags this as an error — the files' values in summary.json are authoritative.)

8) ASSUMPTIONS EACH NUMBER RESTS ON: 759/759 rests on stride-20 sampling of 15,164 records over the ~8-day DAS window being representative (sampled fraction ≈ 3.3% of time). Anomalies rest on robust z-score per feature with threshold z > 5.0. Catalog Σ and P(Mw≥5.5) rest on the 5-event LBNL/NCEDC catalogue (extremely small sample) and the assumed b values; p_per_year assumes the observed window scales linearly to a year (62 events × scaling → 1870.77/yr); p_if_pohang_volume uses V = 12,800 m³ (Pohang). The DAS upper bound assumes every DAS detection counts as M ≥ mc (−0.48) with relative magnitudes — hence over-counting. Context: pumping (GDR 917) 2016-03-11→03-27, net injected −40,484.9 m³; hourly Spearman events_vs_net_injection = −0.173. Pohang reference: sigma_range [−2.0,−1.0], b [0.65,0.73], Mw 5.5; Σ needed at Brady for 1% Mw≥5.5 over the observed volume: −2.17 (b=1.0), −3.65 (b=0.73), −4.09 (b=0.65) — the site Σ (−5.45…−5.28) is already far below these. interpretation.md's prose contains three flagged errors (stride "20 s" should be every 20th record; the calibration note is reversed; the Σ comparison sentence is backwards) — the values reported above come from summary.json and the CSV/JSONL files, not that prose.
